name: North Face
text: [overview] The N face holds numerous gullies plus snow cols, which offer a fun ascent.
[overview] Crampons and a single axe suit the neve plus soft snow up to the ridge, then trudge to the summit, which is somewhat triangular.
[overview] Snowshoes were used for the stretch between a spot roughly 0.5 miles short of Hell Hole Lake and the foot of the peak.

name: Pipeline Couloir
text: [overview] North-facing diagonal couloir on this pair of peaks, inside Snowbird resort and also a well-known ski descent.
[overview] It also makes a good snow/alpine objective later in the season.
[approach] The couloir cuts the north side of the Twins above Gad Valley at Snowbird.
[approach] Pickets can be useful later in the season when the snow firms up.

name: Veteran Obsession
text: [overview] Work up a small snowfield to the first step, then onward through more snow to a bigger step higher up.
[approach] Veteran Obsession is two short flows on the northwest face, down and left of The Hooker Party, reached by climbing a small snowfield to the first step.

name: Twin Peaks via Broads Fork
text: [approach_variants] Snow can sit in the cirque into summer.
[approach_variants] Lingering snow in the cirque and on the saddle into summer.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — probably wanted on snow

name: North Face Chimney
text: [overview] Pitch 1 (M4, 30m): begin about 5 feet to the chimney's right, traverse left, hook and stem the runnel past snowfields and a bulge that is steep and loose, to an alcove belay.
[overview] Pitch 2 (M4/5.7 R, 60m): traverse left, stem and chimney around a chockstone past a ratty old fixed rope, then moderate snow/mixed to a cave belay.
[approach] In winter and spring the way in is on skis from the Alta base area, through avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast and judge snow stability on the way to the base.

name: Down South
text: [overview] Numerous 4th class ridge pitches, snowy or part snow and part rock, lead to the Monte Cristo south face.
[overview] One party climbed during what were basically winter conditions, using an axe and crampons on the lower pitches in mountain boots;
[overview] the face itself was bare of snow apart from some ledges.

name: Tanner's Gulch
text: [overview] A great snow climb for late spring, usable for reaching Twin Peaks, Sunrise Peak or Dromedary Peak as large ski-mountaineering goals.
[overview] Take the clear snow path up the lower gulch until a fork is reached via easy steps of mixed ground, then take the right fork onto the higher snowfields.
[overview] Cross leftward across them to the upper gulch and ascend snow of moderate steepness to the saddle between Dromedary and Sunrise.
[overview] The last 20 feet below the saddle may be extremely corniced, or snow, or ice.
[approach] Early in the season the gulch is filled with snow from low down;
[approach] Carry an ice axe and crampons, and check the avalanche forecast first, since the gulch is a funnel.
[descent_text] The last stretch below it may be snow, ice or a heavy cornice.
[descent_text] Loose terrain makes the gulch unpleasant on foot when the snow is thin, and avalanche conditions matter either way.

name: Anderson Pass
text: [approach_variants] Snow, when present, only lasts into early summer, and without it the pitch is a steep walk..
[approach_variants] Snow may linger on the upper slopes into early summer.
[overview] Snow climbing up the prominent coulouir seen directly beneath the summit of Kings.
[overview] For more snow, climb the face right of the summit ridge instead.
[overview] Without snow this is a steep hike, while with snow it adds some interest to an otherwise monotonous walk.

name: Northwest Ridge Couloir aka Snack Break Couloir
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe

name: Jedediah
text: [overview] Snow and ice at low angle lead to a vertical pillar, brief and the highlight of the route.
[overview] Snow can hide the chain anchor.

[descent_text] After pulling over the lip of the vertical pillar the ice ends and a short stretch of easy mixed ground leads to a chain anchor on the right, which can be buried in snow, or to a fixed anchor higher and to the left.

name: Champagne Chute
text: [overview] Snow route above Pole Canyon Basin that reaches almost the summit of Nebo;
[overview] the trail to North Peak is there but will probably be under snow, and a very steep snow shoulder might need passing, so use caution.
[detailed_rack] A light technical kit may be nice: a skinny rope, snow anchors and a light rock rack.
[what_to_bring] ice axe.
[what_to_bring] crampons.
[approach] Take an ice axe, crampons, a helmet and avalanche gear.

name: Southeast Ridge
text: [overview] Mixed/alpine route, probably best when colder and snowier.
[overview] Then 50m of third class and moderate snow to a ramp with an obvious tree.
[approach] Start from the Snowbasin base area;

name: Blades Couloir
text: [approach] Carry an ice axe and possibly crampons.
[descent_text] Bum-sliding is popular in good snow, but the couloir has a secondary fall line that pulls you toward the west wall, where sun can open a moat that has caught experienced climbers.
[descent_text] Rocks poke through the snow in places, so keep your axe in hand.

name: Reese Couloir
text: [approach] The couloir is the prominent snow line in the middle of the north face.
[approach] Take an ice axe, and crampons if you want them.
[descent_text] rocks stick up through its snow.
[descent_text] Bum-sliding is popular on Blades in good snow, and in good conditions you can slide from the notch to the waterfall, bypass it on the east side and walk out to Neffs Canyon.
[descent_text] Keep away from the west side where sun forms a moat that can be dangerous.

name: Grunge Couloir
text: [overview] The couloir is a snow chute, steep, at Timpanogos's NE end, giving direct access to the north summit.
[overview] A slide would turn the couloir into a death trap, so snow conditions must be judged ahead of committing to it.
[overview] another is Cold Fusion Couloir, glissaded if it holds snow;
[detailed_rack] a tool could be very handy with firmer snow or if ice appears.
[what_to_bring] crampons — a must

[descent_text] Descend the northwest ridge to a dirt road and walk it back to the car, glissade the neighbouring Cold Fusion couloir if it holds snow, or continue along the summit ridge to the main summit first.

name: North Face Direct
text: [overview] Later pitches need no technical gear, and pitch 1 can be skipped via the snow gully left or by scrambling easier rock right.
[overview] get over the gully, snowy, with care then ascend rock for several hundred feet of height, which gets easier toward the top.
[what_to_bring] ice axe — if the gullies still hold snow, when avoiding pitch 1

name: Mobius Dick
text: [overview] Snow bridges and creek crossings that are frozen split the climb into several small pitches.
[approach] The climb follows the creek, with several short ice steps separated by snow bridges and frozen creek crossings, and it does not form every winter.

name: Turf War
text: [overview] P1 (M5): thin ice and turf smear, then a snow section with a big chimney, the first hard bit;
[overview] P2 (M4): offwidth to a snow field, then right to a belay under a slab leading to a big corner system facing left.
[overview] P3 (M5): steep snow to slab, then the massive corner through a tricky overhang;
[overview] P5 (M3): snow plus simple mixed ground into the trees, atop the north summit.

name: Northwest Face
text: [overview] West Face Ramp is the big snow ramp beside the rock on its right.
[overview] Typically expect about 2-3 pitches mixing rock with snow, then steep snow, then the North Ridge to the summit.

name: Northwest Ramp
text: [overview] West Face Ramp is the big snow ramp beside it on the right.
[overview] Climb the ramp 300' to its apex, then 100' of west-face rock to more snow.

name: Diaphanous Dagger
text: [approach] Diaphanous Dagger is the third gully in from the right, and starts up a snow apron into a narrowing chimney below the ice flow.

name: "Scott-ish" Scratchin'
text: [overview] A decent romp up a snow gully that is steep (sometimes deep), leading to ice pitches in a good year.
[overview] one 70m rappel should land in snow, where you downclimb.
[approach] Scott-ish Scratchin' is the second gully in from the right, running almost parallel to and just after the first, and the way to the ice is up a steep snow gully that can be deep.
[descent_text] There is no tree to thread, so a rappel from the top of the ice lands in snow that you downclimb.

name: Temptation Ridge
text: [overview] Beginning at the trailhead for White Pine, skin or use crampons up the initial slide path, called Scotty's bowl.

name: Higher Grounds
text: [overview] Above pitch 2, aim up-left toward a lone conifer, cross the ledge system leftward to the following snowy weakness, and climb that gully to a short ice pitch just under the ridgeline.

name: Root Canal
text: [overview] Mixed climbing that demands focus comes first, with mellow snow after.

[overview] With a single 70m rope, 3 rappels (2 long, 1 short) went from trees and a block left of the route (climbers left), reaching a snow shoulder at ridge height, where neighboring routes finish.
[overview] Cross the snow leftward to those routes' tops and use their descent.
[descent_text] Rappel from trees and a block to the climber's left of the route until you are on the snow shoulder level with the ridge where the other routes top out.
[descent_text] Traverse left across the snow to the top of those routes and follow their descent.

name: No Bologna
text: [overview] The pseudo-pitch below climbs steep snow in a tight gully, right of the ice, with a few mixed moves past a boulder blocking the line, and ends beneath the obvious roof.
[overview] The ice pitch is the obvious pillar, 35 feet, then easy ice and snow to trees.

name: Trial by Spire
text: [overview] P3 is 80m of snow, kept as far left as possible to limit overhead hazard.
[overview] P4 is 65m of snow and easy mixed.
[overview] P5 is either 140m of steep consequential snow, simul-climbed with a serious fall potential, or 70m M3 up a band of loose rock to the right.
[overview] P6 is 70m of 35 degree snow;

name: The Central Spur
text: [overview] P3 (5.9, 20m): rightward under the roof, 2 bolts, then the snow ramp, ending at a fixed belay on a ledge.
[what_to_bring] ice axe or ski poles — depending on conditions

name: A Day in Scotland
text: [overview] Above, the gully winds around several chockstones and needs varied techniques, with granite slabs in crampons and thin, engaging ice adding to the adventure.
